title: Claire's Recalls Children's Metal Necklaces Due to Risk of Lead Exposure
summary: The recalled necklaces contain high levels of lead. Lead is toxic if ingested by young children and can cause adverse health effects. Units: About 67,000.

title: OKK Trading Recalls Toy TVs Due to Violation of Lead Paint Standard
summary: Surface coating on the toy television could contain excessive levels of lead, violating the federal lead paint standard. Units: About 2,100.

title: Sherwin-Williams Co. Recalls Krylon UV Fabric Protector Due to Respiratory Hazard
summary: Overexposure to fumes, vapor or spray mist from the product can pose a serious respiratory hazard to consumers. Units: About 75,000.

title: Toy Xylophones Recalled by King Import Warehouse Due to Violation of Lead Paint Standard
summary: Surface paint on the toy xylophone contains excessive levels of lead, violating the federal lead paint standard. Units: About 144.

title: Candela Recalls Candles Due to Fire and Burn Hazards; Sold Exclusively at Anthropologie Stores
summary: The candle flames could flare up out of the tin container during the burning of the last half inch of wax, posing a fire and burn hazard. Units: About 225.

title: ImagiPLAY Recalls Bead Maze Toys Due to Laceration Hazard
summary: The trees on the toys can detach, exposing a metal screw. This poses a laceration hazard to young children. Units: About 500.

title: Near Strangulation of Child Prompts Recall to Repair Window Blinds by Green Mountain Vista
summary: The black-out roller shades and insulated Roman shades have a continuous looped bead chain that when not attached to the wall or floor, hangs loosely by the blind, posing a fatal strangulation hazard to children. Units: About 7,300.

title: Strangulation Death of a Child Prompts Recall of Roman Blinds; Sold Exclusively at IKEA
summary: Strangulations can occur when a child places his/her neck in an exposed inner cord on the backside of the roman blinds. Units: About 670,000 (an additional 4.8 million were sold outside of the United States).

title: Watts Water Technologies Recalls Rotor and Shaft Assemblies Due to Fire Hazard
summary: If the assembly was installed in a fire suppression system and remained in a closed position, sufficient water might not have been available in the event of a fire. This posed a fire hazard to consumers. Units: About 15.

title: Brownie's Third Lung Recalls Air Compressors Due to Drowning Hazard
summary: The air compressor's components can fail, which could cause a stoppage of air flow. This poses a risk of drowning to users. Units: About 1,000.

title: Children's Hooded Jackets with Drawstrings Recalled by R&D International Due to Strangulation Hazard
summary: The jackets have drawstrings through the hood and at the waist. Children can get entangled in the drawstrings that can catch on playground equipment, fences or tree branches. Units: About 1,500.

title: Target Recalls Dive Sticks Due to Impalement Hazard
summary: The recalled dive sticks could remain in an upright position, posing an impalement hazard to young children. Units: About 365,000.

title: GE Recalls to Inspect and Repair Wall Ovens Due to Fire and Burn Hazards
summary: The extreme heat used in the self-clean cycle can escape, if the wall oven door is removed and incorrectly re-attached by the installer or the consumer. This can pose a fire and burn hazard to consumers. Units: About 244,000.

title: Lithium-Ion Batteries Used with Bicycle Lights Recalled By DiNotte Lighting Due to Burn Hazard
summary: A loose wiring connection and improper venting can cause the battery to overheat, posing a burn hazard to consumers. Units: About 1,700.

title: Cobra Electronics Recalls Children's Two-Way Radios with Rechargeable Batteries Due to Chemical Burn Hazard; Sold Exclusively in Toys "R" Us Stores
summary: The rechargeable batteries in the radios can leak electrolyte, posing a chemical burn hazard to consumers. Units: About 8,000.

title: JA-RU Recalls Toy Trains Due To Choking Hazard
summary: The recalled toy contain small parts which can detach, posing a choking hazard to young children. Units: About 18,000.

title: Lighted Showcases Recalled by Seventh Avenue Due to Fire Hazard
summary: The lighted showcase's plug adaptor can overheat and melt the adaptor's plastic housing, posing a fire hazard. Units: About 700.

title: Off-Road Motorcycles Recalled by American Honda Motor Due to Risk of Swing Arm Weld Failure
summary: The weld on the right side of the swing arm can fail, causing the rider to lose control and crash. This could pose a risk of injury or death to riders. Units: About 13,000.

title: Swim 'N Score Dive Sticks Recalled by Modell's Due to Risk of Impalement Injury to Children
summary: Children can fall or land on these dive sticks in shallow water and suffer impalement injuries. Eye and other facial injuries are also possible. Units: About 130.

title: Stainless Steel Pots Recalled by Ocean State Jobbers Due to Burn Hazard
summary: The stainless steel pots have metal handles that can detach during use, posing a serious burn hazard to consumers. Units: About 7,000.

title: Heavy Duty Acidic Cleaner Recalled by DuPont Due to Leaking Cap; Poses Risk of Severe Skin Irritation
summary: Pressure can build up in a full or nearly full bottle of the acidic cleaner when it is stored in elevated temperatures over an extended period of time, which can result in the cleaner leaking from underneath the cap. If the product comes into contact with skin, it can cause severe skin irritation. U

title: JCPenney Recalls Arizona® Newborn and Infant Pants Due to Choking Hazard
summary: The metal snap at the waist can detach posing a choking hazard to infants. Units: About 24,000.
